title: Mixing Chinese Idioms with English
synopsis: Recently some Chinese netizens started mixing Chinese idioms with English.

fullText.simplified:
中英混搭的成语

    成语难吗？那如果成语里面有英文呢？
    最近，有网友恶搞成语，把成语和英文结合起来，读起来还挺顺口。比如，他们把“有备而来” 改成“有bear来”，因为“备而”的读音和英文“bear”的读音很像。他们把 “东施效颦”改成“东施shopping”，同样的，是因为“效颦”的读音和“shopping”很像。
    这种混搭一发不可收拾，有网友还把混搭发展到了菜名上。比如，他们把“鱼香肉丝”叫做“鱼香rose”，把“西红柿炒鸡蛋”叫做“西horse炒鸡蛋”。
    更有甚者，还发起了给古代人取英文名。比如，他们叫“汉文帝”“Wendy”，叫“汉景帝”“Kindy”，叫“汉哀帝”“Eddie”……
    那么，你知道下面这些词语应该怎么混搭吗？
    “半途而废”，“倾盆大雨”，“深藏不露”，“三生有幸”，还有菜名“煎饼果子”。
    答案是：“半途而废”—“半tour废”，“倾盆大雨”—“ 倾panda雨”，“深藏不露”—“ 深藏blue”，“三生有幸”—“ Samsung有幸”，“煎饼果子”—“煎bingo子”。
    你答对了吗？你还可以把哪些词语混搭呢？但要注意，这些只是网友的恶搞，千万不要用在正式场合。
fullText.traditional:
中英混搭的成語

    成語難嗎？那如果成語裡面有英文呢？
    最近，有網友惡搞成語，把成語和英文結合起來，讀起來還挺順口。比如，他們把“有備而來” 改成“有bear來”，因為“備而”的讀音和英文“bear”的讀音很像。他們把 “東施效顰”改成“東施shopping”，同樣的，是因為“效顰”的讀音和“shopping”很像。
    這種混搭一發不可收拾，有網友還把混搭發展到了菜名上。比如，他們把“魚香肉絲”叫做“魚香rose”，把“西紅柿炒雞蛋”叫做“西horse炒雞蛋”。
    更有甚者，還發起了給古代人取英文名。比如，他們叫“漢文帝”“Wendy”，叫“漢景帝”“Kindy”，叫“漢哀帝”“Eddie”……
    那麼，你知道下面這些詞語應該怎麼混搭嗎？
    “半途而廢”，“傾盆大雨”，“深藏不露”，“三生有幸”，還有菜名“煎餅果子”。
    答案是：“半途而廢”—“半tour廢”，“傾盆大雨”—“ 傾panda雨”，“深藏不露”—“ 深藏blue”，“三生有幸”—“ Samsung有幸”，“煎餅果子”—“煎bingo子”。
    你答對了嗎？你還可以把哪些詞語混搭呢？但要注意，這些只是網友的惡搞，千萬不要用在正式場合。

raw.synopsis: Recently some Chinese netizens started mixing Chinese idioms with English.
sentence_translations: Chinese Idioms that are Mixed with English Words
Do you think Chinese idioms are hard?
What if they are mixed with English?
Recently, some netizens made fun of some Chinese idioms by mixing them with English.
When you read them they still sound quite fluent.
For example, the idiom “To come prepared” is changed to “A bear comes”,
Because the two characters in the middle “bei er” sound similar to the English word “bear”.
The idiom “Dong Shi’s imitation” was changed to “Dong Shi's shopping”.
Because in the same way the pronunciation of “xiao ping” is similar to the word “shopping”.
This type of mixed phrases soon went viral, and some netizens even began to make fun of names of dishes.
For example, they turned “fish-flavored shredded pork” into “fish-flavored rose”, ..
.. and “tomato and scrambled eggs” into “western horse with scrambled eggs”.
Some people even gave English names to people from ancient eras.
For example, instead of “Emperor Wen of Han” they say “Wendy”.
For “Emperor Jing of Han” they say “Kindy”,  and “Emperor Ai of Han” becomes “Eddie”.
So, do you know how to mix the following phrases with English?
“Giving up halfway”, “rain pouring like from a basin”, “deeply hidden and never shown”, ..
.. “the blessing of thee lifetimes” and the name of the dish “fruity pancake”.
The answers are: “giving up halfway” — “giving up half-tour”,
“rain pouring like from a tilted basin” — “tilted panda rain”,
“deeply hidden and never shown” — “deeply hidden blue”,
“the blessing of thee lifetimes” — “the blessing of Samsung”,
“fruity pancake” – “fried bingo”.
Did you get them right?
Can you mix any other Chinese idioms with English?
But note that these are just for fun, and you should never use them at formal occasions.
